name: Georgia

context: GA 380: Windbreaks reduce wind erosion; barrier density at least 65 percent, and the protected area falls within 10H of the design height.
GA 329: Use the current approved wind erosion prediction technology to set the surface residue needed, its timing and allowed soil disturbance.
cover_rules: GA 340: Cover crop termination may not be earlier than 30 days before cash crop planned planting date or cover crop flowering whatever is first.
GA 340: Rates are for drilling; if broadcasting, plant the maximum rate and increase it by 15 to 20 percent.
residue: GA 329: Use current wind erosion prediction technology to determine the randomly distributed surface residue needed and when it must be present.
GA 345: Use current wind erosion prediction technology to determine the field operations that leave the residue needed.
windbreak: GA 380: Orient the windbreak as close to perpendicular to the troublesome wind as possible; minimum barrier density 65 percent.
seeding: GA 340: Seeding rates are for drilling and are based on average purity and germination, not pure live seed (PLS).
GA 340: For aerial application, increase seeding rates by 30 percent.
disturbed: GA 342: Critical area planting applies to highly disturbed areas such as mined lands, construction areas and eroded channel banks.
GA 342: Mulch or otherwise stabilize (e.g., polyacrylamide (PAM)) plantings as necessary to ensure successful establishment.

cover.name: Small grains (Oats, Rye, Wheat, barley, Triticale)

coverPlant.text: GA 340: Small grains are seeded Sep 1 – Nov 1 (Mountains), Sep 15 – Nov 1 (Piedmont), Sep 15 – Dec 15 (Coastal Plains).
GA 340: Browntop Millet, Sorghum-Sudan and Soybean are seeded Apr 1-Aug 15 in the Coastal Plains (May 1–Aug 1 in the Mountains).

seedWin.text: GA 340: Cool-season cover crops such as Crimson Clover are seeded Sep 1 – Oct 15 (Piedmont), Sep 15 –Dec 1 (Coastal Plains).
GA 340: Cowpeas are seeded May 1-June 15 in the Mountains and Piedmont, May 1-July 15 in the Coastal Plains.
